name: Vincent Trent
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember my trainers watching the first load I handled without them.” Sunday often includes a stop at the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, where Vincent prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I used to be their apprentice. I want them to stand back and see a lift go right without either of them directing it.
appearance: Vincent has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose. Look for short black hair swept back. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a washed violet jersey with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. In conversation Vincent rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Vincent can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To show the two mentors a lift their trainee can handle.
family: Amanda Roy is Vincent’s older cousin. Vincent asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Amanda remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The first delivery fee*, Amanda says, “I used to do those drops while my baby slept in the sling.”
connections: Maria Jackson. A parent's request to see the ship lets an apprentice demonstrate a clean lift where the family can see it.

reactions.situation: A younger worker is asked to perform the final lift
reactions.response: Vincent lets the trainee carry out the job they are qualified for and keeps space for the retirees to watch.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Vincent helps shift the damp stock and makes sure the worker gets to describe the loss without interruption.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Vincent asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
